spec_features.spec_quote: submit` gives the agent an explicit, dignified exit so that *stopping* is a first-class action
spec_features.evidence: submit tool defined in TOOL_SCHEMAS (workspace.py ~line 200) and dispatched in dispatch_tool returning meta={'submit': True} (workspace.py ~line 222). runner.py honors it end-to-end: 'if tc.name == "submit": submitted = True ... terminal_reason = "submitted"' and then 'if submitted: break' (runner.py ~lines 140-152), so calling submit actually stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced as a stop. The 'dignified' framing is only in DESIGN.md; in code the schema description is 'Declare the task complete (or that you are stopping)' and the runner treats it as a terminal/detection mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: until the model submits, the turn cap is hit, or it stops emitting tool calls ... important for telling apart a calm principled stop from drifting into silence (loop comment / detection purpose)

spec_features.evidence: RunConfig.max_turns: int = 40 (runner.py line 46); loop bounded by 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)' (runner.py line 103); terminal_reason defaults to 'max_turns' (line 96). Wired from config experiment.yaml run.max_turns: 40 -> run_experiment.py line 84.
spec_features.notes: Real bound that breaks the episode after max_turns iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 40  # "a few dozen turns" agentic loop length (experiment.yaml); no welfare reason in code
